content:
simon: heads-up — saw a p99 jump during the 03:04 burst on prod. p50 stayed ~70ms but p99 hit ~2200ms for a short window. KV hitrate tanked to ~11%

maria: ugh. any idea if this was scale-up lag or kernel choice flip?

simon: looks like a combo. autoscaler prober smoothed the signal, so we scaled a bit later than the traffic spike. when new pods came up their KV caches were empty and kernel-selector picked a fallback kernel for short sequences. net: cold KV misses + slightly slower kernel = tail outlier.

aj: can you paste the metrics/queries?

simon: prometheus snippets I pulled:

```
# kv hitrate (1m)
sum(rate(inference_kv_hit_total[1m])) / sum(rate(inference_kv_request_total[1m]))
\n# p99 generation latency across pool (5m)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_generation_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool))
```

simon: at the spike we saw kv hitrate drop from ~85% -> 11% in ~40s, and the kernel selection histogram showed a transient shift to the compatible-fallback path for ~70% of requests.

lina: that kernel fallback is expected when weight sampler has low samples for sequence-length buckets. maybe microbatching heuristics also influenced it — if microbatch size was clamped down on cold nodes, selector bias changes.

aj: quick mitigation options I see:
- reduce prober smoothing alpha (react faster)
- add short-lived prewarm container that keeps KV warm for Xs after scale-down
- bias kernel selector to prefer low-latency variant for seq_len < 64

maria: tradeoffs: faster prober = more churn and cost; prewarm = idle GPU time; kernel bias = potential regen quality mismatch. need experiment plan + metrics to watch.

simon: agree. proposed quick experiment (canary):
- prober.smoothing = 0.1 (was 0.3)
- prewarm.idle_ttl = 45s (was 10s)
- kernel.selector.bias.short_seq = "prefer-low-latency"
- lower microbatch.min_size on new nodes to 2 -> let batching fill in as cache warms

aj: config snippet for rollout (canary):
```
{
  "name": "probe-smoothing-canary-1",
  "fraction": 0.05,
  "changes": {
    "prober.smoothing": 0.1,
    "prewarm.idle_ttl": 45,
    "kernel.selector.bias": "low_latency_short_seq"
  }
}
```

maria: metrics to collect during canary:
- p50/p95/p99 gen latency per pool
- kv hitrate (1m + 5m)
- kernel distribution by seq_len bucket
- scale-up time (pod create -> ready)
- cost delta (approx GPU-seconds)

opsbot: :white_check_mark: scheduled canary rollout at 06:15 across 5% pool capacity

infra-bot: INFO: canary deployment created: probe-smoothing-canary-1 (id: c-196780-01)

simon: I'll run a targeted load test after deploy if we need to force a burst. plan to capture p99 heatmap and kv hit traces.

lina: small note — if kernel bias causes quality regression on longer sequences we should gate with eval prompts. add an eval job that compares token-level perplexity on a small corpus.

maria: agreed. also add a short-term dashboard: tail heatmap + kv hit fraction + kernel mix. I'll assemble it.

simon: thanks. action items:
- aj: push canary JSON and monitor autoscaler logs (you got infra perms)
- maria: dash and eval job
- lina: quick check on kernel perf delta for seq<64 vs seq>=64 (microbench)

aj: pushing now. will report back with first 30m window.

opsbot: :rocket: aj started canary rollout (5%).

simon: good. if this fixes tail without large cost increase we should consider making prewarm default for burstable pools. otherwise fallback to exploring better prober heuristics (adaptive smoothing + burst detector).

maria: noted, will post dashboard link once live.

simon: thanks team, will update thread with results. :thumbsup:
